The '''bunkbed conjecture''' (also spelled '''bunk bed conjecture''') is a statement in [[percolation theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]] that studies the behavior of connected clusters in a [[random graph]]. The [[conjecture]] is named after its analogy to a [[bunk bed]] structure. It was first posited by [[Pieter Kasteleyn]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=van den Berg |first1=Jacob |last2=Kahn |first2=Jeff |date=2001 |title=A correlation inequality for connection events in percolation |journal=Annals of Probability |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=123–126 |doi=10.1214/aop/1008956324 |jstor=2652916 }}</ref> In 2024, Nikita Gladkov, [[Igor Pak]], and Alexander Zimin gave a counter-example to the bunkbed conjecture, proving that it is false.<ref name="disproof">{{cite journal |arxiv=2410.02545 |author1=Nikita Gladkov |author2=Igor Pak |title=The bunkbed conjecture is false |date=2025 |author3=Aleksandr Zimin |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=122 |issue=24 |article-number=e2420725122 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2420725122 |bibcode=2025PNAS..12220725G }}</ref><ref name="gladkov2025">{{cite journal |last1=Gladkov |first1=Nikita |last2=Pak |first2=Igor |last3=Zimin |first3=Aleksandr |date=2025 |title=The bunkbed conjecture is false |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=122 |issue=24 |article-number=e2420725122 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2420725122 |pmid=40512791 |pmc=12184427 |bibcode=2025PNAS..12220725G |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="quanta">{{Cite web |last=Howlett |first=Joseph |date=2024-11-01 |title=Math's 'Bunkbed Conjecture' Has Been Debunked |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/maths-bunkbed-conjecture-has-been-debunked-20241101/ |access-date=2024-11-02 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==

The conjecture has many equivalent formulations.<ref name= equiv>{{cite journal |last1=Rudzinski |first1=James |last2=Smyth |first2=Clifford |date=2016 |title=Equivalent Formulations of the Bunk Bed Conjecture |url=https://libjournal.uncg.edu/ncjms/article/view/1345 |journal=North Carolina Journal of Mathematics and Statistics |volume=2 |pages=23–28 |doi= |access-date=December 17, 2023}}</ref> In the most general formulation it involves two identical [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]s, referred to as the ''upper bunk'' and the ''lower bunk''. These graphs are [[Graph isomorphism|isomorphic]], meaning they share the same structure. Additional edges, termed ''posts'', are added to connect each vertex in the upper bunk with the corresponding vertex in the lower bunk.

Each edge in the graph is assigned a [[probability]]. The edges in the upper bunk and their corresponding edges in the lower bunk share the same probability. The probabilities assigned to the posts can be arbitrary.

A random subgraph of the bunkbed graph is then formed by independently deleting each edge based on the assigned probability.

Equivalently, it can be assumed that all edges have the same deletion probability <math>0<p<1</math>.<ref name=equiv/>

The bunkbed conjecture states that in the resulting random subgraph, the probability that a vertex {{Mvar|x}} in the upper bunk is connected to some vertex {{Mvar|y}} in the upper bunk is greater than or equal to the probability that {{Mvar|x}} is connected to {{Math|''y&prime;''}}, the isomorphic copy of {{Mvar|y}} in the lower bunk.

== Interpretation and significance ==

The conjecture suggests that two vertices of a graph are more likely to remain connected after randomly removing some edges if the graph distance between the vertices is smaller. This is intuitive, and similar questions for [[Random_walk#On_graphs|random walks]] and [[Ising model]] were resolved positively.<ref name=Hag98>{{cite journal |last1=Häggström |first1=Olle |date=1998 |title=On a conjecture of Bollobás and Brightwell concerning random walks on product graphs |journal=Combinatorics, Probability and Computing |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=397–401 |doi= 10.1017/S0963548398003605|arxiv=}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Häggström |first1=Olle |date=2003 |title=Probability on bunkbed graphs |journal=Proceedings of FPSAC |volume=3 |issue= |pages=19–27 |doi= |arxiv=}}</ref> The original motivation for the conjecture was its implication that, in a percolation on the infinite square grid, the probability of {{Math|(0, 0)}} being connected to {{Math|(''x'', ''y'')}} for {{Math|''x'', ''y'' &ge; 0}} is greater than the probability of {{Math|(0, 0)}} being connected to {{Math|(''x'' + 1, ''y'')}}.<ref name=Hag98 />

It was [[mathematical proof|proved]] for specific types of graphs, such as [[Wheel graph|wheels]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Leander |first1=Madeleine |date=2009 |title=On the bunkbed conjecture |url=https://kurser.math.su.se/pluginfile.php/16103/mod_folder/content/0/2009/2009_07_report.pdf |journal=Självständiga arbeten i matematik |pages= |doi= |access-date=December 17, 2023}}</ref> [[Complete graph|complete]] graphs,<ref>{{cite journal
	| last1 = van Hintum
	| first1 = Peter |last2 = Lammers | first2 = Piet 
	| date = 2018
	| title = The bunkbed conjecture on the complete graph
	| journal = European Journal of Combinatorics | volume = 76 | pages = 175–177 | doi = 10.1016/j.ejc.2018.10.002 | arxiv = 1803.07647
	}}</ref> [[Complete bipartite graph|complete bipartite]] graphs, and graphs with a local symmetry.<ref>{{cite arXiv
	| last = Richthammer
	| first = Thomas
	| date = 2022
	| title = Bunkbed conjecture for complete bipartite graphs and related classes of graphs
	| eprint = 2204.12931
	| class = math.PR
}}</ref> It was also proved in the limit {{Math|''p'' &rightarrow; 1}} for any graph.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hutchcroft |first1=Tom |last2=Kent |first2=Alexander |last3=Nizić-Nikolac |first3=Petar |date=2023 |title=The bunkbed conjecture holds in the ''p''↑1 limit|url= https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/172974/1/WRAP-bunkbed-conjecture-holds-limit-2023.pdf|journal=Combinatorics, Probability and Computing |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=363–369 |doi=10.1017/S096354832200027X  |publisher=Cambridge University Press|s2cid=263889353 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv
	| last = Hollom
	| first = Lawrence
	| date = 2023
	| title = A new proof of the bunkbed conjecture in the ''p''↑1 limit
	| eprint = 2302.00031
	| class = math.CO
}}</ref>

[[File:Bunkbed counterexample for hypergraphs.svg|thumb|A counterexample for [[hypergraph]]s where each bunk has 10 vertices and 6 hyperedges of order 3. If all hyperedges and the indicated posts are selected with probability {{sfrac|1|2}}, vertices 1 and 10' are slightly more likely to be connected than 1 and 10.<ref name=hollom2024>{{cite arXiv |last=Hollom |first=Lawrence |title=The bunkbed conjecture is not robust to generalisation |date=2024-06-03 |class=math.CO |eprint=2406.01790}}</ref> The original disproof to the standard bunkbed conjecture is based on this counterexample.<ref name="disproof"/>]]

Counterexamples for generalizations of the bunkbed conjecture have been published for site percolation, [[hypergraph]]s, and [[directed graph]]s.<ref name=hollom2024/> The original disproof is based on a small counterexample in the 3-uniform hypergraph case with 10 vertices; the counterexample for the standard bunkbed conjecture with all edge probabilities equal to {{sfrac|1|2}} (equivalent to the general case) has a [[planar graph|planar]] bunk with 7222 vertices and 14442 edges, and where there is an {{mvar|x}} and {{mvar|y}} where connecting {{mvar|x}} to {{math|''y&prime;''}} is more probable by around <math>10^{-6509}</math>. They also show that there is a counterexample in the general case with 28 vertices and 54 edges on the bunk and an {{mvar|x}} and {{mvar|y}} where difference in probabilities of around <math>10^{-78}</math> in favor of  {{mvar|x}} to {{math|''y&prime;''}}.<ref name="disproof"/><ref name="gladkov2025"/>
